claim_one_line: THE ALREADY-BANKED CHECK -- the finished-but-forgotten class gets an INSTRUMENT, not a promise. THE FAILURE, FOUR TIMES, ALWAYS THE SAME SHAPE: a REGISTER row said open while the CORPUS already held the proof -- 'QP-1 (the quine) open' while B762 had proved it (months); L187's 'none has been executed' while B767 had run six of seven (~5 weeks); 'the F2/F8 locks are missing' while B1003 had banked them (~3 weeks); R5's 'the proof is a NAMED OPEN STEP... no successor' while B775/B778 had proved it for all p (~5 weeks). Every one would have been caught by SEARCHING THE CORPUS INSTEAD OF READING THE REGISTER. Review 52 raised the class to a standing audit item; an audit item is not an instrument -- this is the instrument. WHAT IT IS: scripts/checks/already_banked.py scans EVERY frontier/*/arc_verdict.json AND every nested FINDINGS.md (the cell-level files where B775/B778 lived, which arc-level scans miss), ranks by term coverage, and EXITS NON-ZERO if any arc in a settled state (PROVED/NEGATIVE/RESOLVED/RESOLVED-A/THEOREM/RETRACTED) matches a real share of the query. THE THRESHOLD IS THE LOAD-BEARING DESIGN: a first version flagged any settled arc sharing ONE incidental word, which would fire on everything -- and an instrument that cries wolf gets ignored, which is precisely how the four misses happened; the rule is now matches >= max(2, ceil(terms/2)). CONTROLS, TWO-SIDED: positive -- all FOUR real historical misses are FLAGGED, each surfacing at top rank the exact arc that was missed; negative -- two regions the existence audit established as genuinely blind (inflation/reheating/e-folds; dark matter/relic abundance/freeze-out) come back CLEAN, so a MISSING claim there remains admissible. An instrument that only fired would be useless; this one discriminates. THE RULE IT ENFORCES, added to WORKING_RULES: no MISSING/OPEN/'never run'/'no successor' claim is admissible until the check has been run on its terms, and the SEARCHED TERMS ARE STATED WITH THE CLAIM; folded into the review checklist beside VERIFY-THE-VERIFIER. FENCES: the check is a RETRIEVAL aid, not an adjudicator -- a flagged hit means read that arc before writing 'missing', not that the claim is wrong; term matching is lexical, so a claim phrased in vocabulary absent from the corpus can still slip -- the check REDUCES the class, it does not abolish it, and the honest response to a clean result is 'no settled arc matched THESE TERMS', which is what the tool prints. Gate 5 clean.
